topic: Leading and Empowering Global Teams during a Pandemic
title: Leading and Empowering Global Teams during a Pandemic
session_title: Lessons learnt from Effectively Managing Projects and Teams during a Global Pandemic
abstract: After almost two years of a global pandemic, businesses and life in general have had to adapt to a new normal. Most of us found ways to effectively perform our jobs from a forced work-from-home environment, but did we do it right? Did we lose something more than the casual coffee chat with colleagues at the office? Did we lead our teams in an effective way? In this talk, we will discuss and reflect on a few examples from ExxonMobil.

topic: Navigating the COVID-19 Pandemic at Michigan Technological University
title: Navigating the COVID-19 Pandemic at Michigan Technological University
session_title: Lessons learnt from Effectively Managing Projects and Teams during a Global Pandemic
abstract: Very few could have imagined that in early 2020 the novel coronavirus would upend the normal life (including academia) in the US. During the 2020 spring break, it was decided that students would not return to campus, and that all classes would be taught remotely for the remainder of the spring term. The campus was shut down in the third week of March 2020, with no access to offices and other campus facilities. Most research laboratories were also shuttered. This shutdown presented several challenges both at the administration level and at the academic unit level. Very few faculty members had the knowledge and experience of teaching an on-line course. With no historical precedent to guide a situation like this, the academic community had to adjust and adapt quickly. A decision was made to offer classes in blended mode (i.e., in-person + remote) for the 2020-2021 academic year. The efforts during summer 2020 included (i) training faculty for online teaching, (ii) scheduling courses in blended mode while following the CDC safety protocols, and (iii) making special provisions for teaching the Unit Operations Laboratory courses while still preserving hands-on experiential learning. Both the UO Laboratory and capstone senior design courses also overcame the challenge of holding help/review and presentation sessions for student teams. The efforts across the curriculum were made to accommodate students who required isolation because of symptoms or possible exposure to COVID-19 and to provide remote access to design software. Overall, it has been nothing less than a Herculean effort to pull this off successfully. This presentation will share the challenges and operational details and provide insights into those changes that will become permanent enhancements to the program.

topic: Managing Teams Effectively during a Pandemic Required – Empathy, Connection, Agility, Prioritization and Support
title: Managing Teams Effectively during a Pandemic Required – Empathy, Connection, Agility, Prioritization and Support

abstract: COVID-19 Global Pandemic has catalyzed growth in leadership behaviors and effectiveness. Progressing on innovation goals while prioritizing employee and customer experiences has required new approaches and solutions. We will discuss examples from Dow Industrial Solutions R&D that focused on Empathy, Connection, Agility, Prioritization and Support.

topic: Lessons learned from field testing a new technology during the pandemic
title: Lessons learned from field testing a new technology during the pandemic
session_title: Lessons learnt from Effectively Managing Projects and Teams during a Global Pandemic
abstract: During 2020 and 2021, NICE America conducted field tests of a new hydrogen refueling technology during two separate campaigns, each lasting over three months. During normal times, this endeavor would have required coordination of a multinational team spread across three time zones, safe execution of an ambitious technical validation program, and management of expectations for internal and external stakeholders (including potential customers). The pandemic introduced additional challenges including compliance with evolving public health regulations, constraints on travel and scheduling, and supply chain stress associated with economic consequences of pandemic response. This presentation will describe the actual campaigns, review lessons learned from adapting to the evolving situations, and highlight effective practices that can be generalized for field testing under less extreme circumstances.
presenting_author: Anthony Ku | NICE America Research, Mountain View
